sections.h2: Where is Monroeville, Pennsylvania, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Monroeville is a home rule municipality in Allegheny County, a suburb east of Pittsburgh with 28,640 residents in the 2020 census. It covers about 19.7 square miles, and its elevation ranges from 735 to 1,319 feet, so many streets run up and down hillsides rather than across flat grid blocks.

The municipality touches nine neighbors: Plum to the north, Murrysville, Penn Township and Trafford in Westmoreland County to the east and south, North Versailles, Wilmerding and Turtle Creek to the southwest, Wilkins Township to the west and Penn Hills to the northwest. The borough of Pitcairn sits entirely inside Monroeville, near the south-southwest edge, so a mailing address or a street that looks like Monroeville may actually belong to Pitcairn. Check the parcel record before you quote taxes or rules to a buyer.

sections.h2: How did Monroeville become a municipality?
sections.html:
The area takes its name from Joel Monroe, its first postmaster, and was settled in the mid to late 1800s. It was organized as Patton Township in 1849, became the borough of Monroeville on January 25, 1951, and adopted a Home Rule Charter on May 21, 1974.

Growth followed the highways and the retail boom. Population rose from 22,446 in 1960 to 29,011 in 1970 and 30,977 in 1980, then slipped to 28,386 by 2010 and 28,640 in 2020. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 27,685, about 3.3 percent below the 2020 base. That slow, flat pattern means most homes here belong to established neighborhoods rather than new subdivisions, and many were built in the decades when the population was climbing.

sections.h2: What drives Monroeville's economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Monroeville is best known for the Monroeville Mall, the surrounding office parks and a cluster of high-rise hotels that went up from the 1960s onward. The Monroeville Convention Center, once called the ExpoMart, sits near the mall. U.S. Steel's research laboratory here employed nearly 1,800 people at its 1979 peak.

The Census Bureau reports retail sales of about $2.59 billion in 2022, which works out to $91,813 per resident. That is a measure of how much of the area's activity comes from shopping and services used by people living outside the municipality. Health care and social assistance receipts were about $1.0 billion the same year.

For a seller, the practical effect is that a house near the commercial corridor sits next to heavy traffic and noise, while streets farther back from U.S. 22 trade on quiet and school boundaries.

sections.html:

With nearly a quarter of residents 65 or older and an average household of 2.20 people, many Monroeville houses are larger than their current owners need. Owners without a mortgage pay a median of just $611 a month in housing costs, so a long-held home can be cheap to keep and still need expensive repairs.

sections.h2: Does Monroeville require an occupancy permit when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Yes. Monroeville requires a residential occupancy permit tied to the sale, and an inspection has to be completed before the new owners occupy the home. The municipality's application sets the fee at $100 for a single-family dwelling or townhome, and a second reinspection can add $50 under the municipal fee schedule.

The application works like this:

  • The current owner or the owner's agent files it.
  • It lists the property address, the buyer's name, who will meet the inspector and whether the electricity is on or off.
  • It has a line to mark the house as being sold as is.
  • The permit is issued in the name of the new owners who will live there.

Call the Monroeville building and code office at 412-856-3340 before listing so the inspection can be scheduled early. Utilities that are shut off can delay it, and an inspection that finds problems adds time before a closing date can be set.

sections.h2: What rules apply if the Monroeville house is a rental?
sections.html:
Rental units need their own occupancy permit, and an inspection must be completed before a tenant moves in. The fee is $75 for multi-family units and $100 for a single-family dwelling or townhome, and the permit is issued in the tenant's name. Units occupied before inspection can face penalty fines under the municipal ordinance.

That matters when you sell a house with a tenant in place. Ask the municipality whether the current permit is up to date, and give a buyer who plans to keep the tenant the paperwork. A buyer who intends to rent the house after closing has to apply under the rental rules, separate from the sale permit. If the tenant is leaving anyway, agree on a move-out date in writing so the sale inspection can go ahead on an empty house.

sections.h2: What does a Monroeville sale cost in transfer tax, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax in Monroeville totals 2.5 percent of the price. Allegheny County lists a 1 percent municipal tax and a one-half percent school district tax for Monroeville and the Gateway school district, on top of the 1 percent state tax. The county collects it when the deed is recorded, with a separate check from the recording fees. Certain family transfers can be exempt, and a Statement of Value (form REV-183) covers deeds that list no price.

Assessment appeals go to the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review, the first level of appeal in Allegheny County. Hearings are held by telephone, and an owner may attend alone, hire an attorney or name an authorized representative. If the board's decision is unsatisfactory, the next step is the Court of Common Pleas through the Board of Viewers. School districts and municipalities can also appeal an assessment, and the owner may but does not have to attend those hearings.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Monroeville house quickly?
sections.html:
Speed depends on the inspection, the title and the buyer's financing. A cash purchase of a house as it stands removes the financing step, though the municipal occupancy inspection still applies.

  • Order the occupancy inspection early and fix any items it flags.
  • Pull the Allegheny County parcel record to confirm the owner of record and the school district.
  • Gather payoff figures for any mortgage or lien, and keep the electricity on for the inspector.
  • Compare a listing, a cash offer and an as-is sale to an investor against the repair cost.

Monroeville's location beside I-376, the Pennsylvania Turnpike and U.S. 22 is a selling point for commuters, so photographs and a clear price matter more than staging.

faqs.q: What is the occupancy permit fee when selling a house in Monroeville?
faqs.a: The fee is $100 for a single-family house or townhome, set by the municipal fee schedule. A second reinspection can add $50. The inspection has to be completed before the buyers move in.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Monroeville sale?
faqs.a: It totals 2.5 percent: 1 percent to the state, 1 percent to the municipality and one-half percent to the Gateway school district. Allegheny County collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Is Monroeville a city or a borough?
faqs.a: Monroeville is a home rule municipality in Allegheny County. It was organized as Patton Township in 1849, became a borough in 1951 and adopted a Home Rule Charter in 1974.
The Gateway School District serves students from kindergarten through grade 12. The Allegheny County transfer tax table lists it as the Monroeville-Gateway district for the municipality.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Monroeville property assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the Allegheny County Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review, which holds its hearings by telephone. You can represent yourself, hire an attorney or appoint an authorized representative.
